title: Still No Word
description:
Scrolling Instagram before sleep.
College classmate — promoted to team lead. Old friend — engagement announcement. Elementary school kid who sat behind you — launched a business.
Numbers accumulate. Likes, congratulations, 'so inspiring's.
{name} turns off the screen and stares at the ceiling.

choices.text: Move on. Everyone has their own pace.  (acceptance / numbness)
choices.result_text:
{name} placed the phone face-down and tried to sleep.
Everyone has their own speed — knowing that didn't make the night shorter.

choices.text: Leave genuine congratulations on each post.  (relationship / self-comparison)
choices.result_text:
{name} read every post and left real comments. Meant it.
Happy for them — and something else underneath that was hard to name.

choices.text: Delete the app. For now.  (self-protection / isolation)
choices.result_text:
{name} held down the icon and pressed delete.
Instantly lighter. Some connections might thin out — right now, that was fine.

title: Standing at the Fridge
description:
1 a.m. Hungry.
Open the fridge — half a bag of frozen dumplings, gochujang, two old eggs.
Somewhere along the way, {name} stopped doing proper grocery runs.
Not sure if this counts as frugality or giving up.

choices.text: Microwave the dumplings.  (just deal with it / health)
choices.result_text:
{name} pulled out the dumplings and hit start.
The skin came out rubbery. Still warm.
Not rice, not anything special — just the end of another day.

choices.text: Walk to the convenience store. Eat something real.  (comfort / expense)
choices.result_text:
Two triangle kimbap, one cup noodle. The staff said 'enjoy your meal.'
Ramen at 1 a.m. under fluorescent lights — it was comfort in its own way.

choices.text: Just sleep. Eat tomorrow morning.  (save money / sleep disrupted)
choices.result_text:
{name} shut the fridge and lay down.
Stomach said no. Delivery fee said no louder.
Sleep came late.

title: No Umbrella
description:
The forecast said clear.
Step out of the subway exit — and it's pouring.
Umbrella at home. Important documents in the bag.
{name} stands under the overhang, watching other people walk past with umbrellas.

choices.text: Just run. Getting wet is better.  (fast solution / health)
choices.result_text:
{name} put the bag over their head and sprinted.
Arrived half-soaked. Documents survived. Pants did not.
Embarrassing — also kind of funny.

choices.text: Buy a convenience store umbrella.  (solution / expense)
choices.result_text:
3,000 won vinyl umbrella. Felt disposable — but stayed dry.
Spending 3,000 won to not get rained on is not a bad trade.

choices.text: Wait it out. Watch the rain.  (patience / time)
choices.result_text:
{name} stood under the overhang and watched.
For a moment, the world stopped pressing. Just the sound of rain.
It cleared in an hour.

title: Class Reunion Invite
description:
A notification from the high school group chat.
"Reunion — third Saturday next month. Restaurant in Gangnam. 50,000 won per person."

How do you explain your situation to these people right now?
Skip and it's weird. Go and it's comparisons.

choices.text: Go. You'll run into them eventually.  (connection / expense + stress)
choices.result_text:
{name} went. Uncomfortable at first.
But then someone passed makgeolli and the conversation just happened — a flash of the old days.
50,000 won well spent.

choices.text: Quietly decline.  (save / social distance)
choices.result_text:
"Can't make it" — one line and close the chat.
A few people asked where you were going. Gave a vague answer.
Relieved not to go — and slightly hollow at the same time.

choices.text: Show up briefly and leave early.  (compromise / half-measure)
choices.result_text:
{name} stayed an hour. Said hello to a few people, matched the energy, slipped out.
Not quite there, not quite absent.

title: Landlord's Call
description:
A call from the landlord.
"Prices have gone up everywhere, so I'll need to raise the rent at renewal.
Just 150,000 won more. Everywhere's the same."

150,000 won. More than the monthly electric bill.
Moving costs money too — and cheap options have dried up.

choices.text: Accept it. Moving is harder.  (realistic / expense)
choices.result_text:
{name} agreed.
Deposit, moving costs — the raise was easier.
Just 150,000 won more to earn each month.

choices.text: Negotiate. Suggest 50,000 won instead.  (pushback / relationship awkwardness)
choices.result_text:
{name} carefully said, "150,000 won is difficult — would 50,000 won work?"
The landlord paused. "How about 70,000 won?"
Awkward, but less of an increase.

choices.text: Find a new place. Look for something cheaper.  (freedom / moving cost)
choices.result_text:
Decided to move. Three weeks of searching.
Found something slightly farther and slightly smaller for roughly the same money.
Moving cost more. Still felt like a choice.

title: Apartment Hunting
description:
Three apartments today.
First — bathroom next to the kitchen. Second — no natural light. Third — decent conditions, but for that price in that neighborhood, the money could go elsewhere.

The agent said, "You won't find better at this price range."
{name} stood in each empty room, trying to picture living there.

choices.text: Sign the third one. Best conditions.  (move / expense)
choices.result_text:
Signed.
Moving day — surprisingly little stuff. The empty room looked bigger than expected.
Mine.

choices.text: Keep looking. No need to rush.  (patience / opportunity cost)
choices.result_text:
{name} told the agent, "I'll think about it."
A few days later, someone else signed that apartment.
Didn't love it — but losing it stung anyway.

title: The Results
description:
The national health checkup results came back.
Most things: normal. One item — marked 'borderline.'
The doctor said, "Nothing urgent yet, but you need to change your lifestyle.
Sleep, diet, exercise."

{name} knows. Just hasn't been doing any of it.

choices.text: Take it seriously. Change the routine.  (health investment / time)
choices.result_text:
{name} started walking in the evenings that same day. Cut late-night snacks.
No dramatic changes. Just a little — the body started feeling different.

choices.text: Acknowledge it and forget it. Later.  (reality / neglect)
choices.result_text:
Filed the results in a drawer.
The next checkup, same conversation.

choices.text: Get further testing. Want to know exactly.  (information / cost)
choices.result_text:
Detailed results: still okay. But 'what you do now matters most.'
Spent money, but felt lighter.

title: First Payday
description:
The deposit came through.
Staring at the number — it didn't feel real.
People say you're supposed to take your parents out for a meal on your first paycheck.
{name} looked at the account screen for a long time.

choices.text: Take the parents out for dinner. Small gesture.  (filial duty / expense)
choices.result_text:
A nearby BBQ place. The three of them ate.
Father asked, "How's the food?" Same as always.
On the walk home, {name} nearly cried.

choices.text: Just save it. That's the real gift.  (frugality / goal)
choices.result_text:
{name} hit the transfer button.
To savings. No fanfare — just the first investment in yourself.

choices.text: Spend some on yourself. Just this once.  (self-reward / expense)
choices.result_text:
{name} bought something long put off. Nothing extravagant.
But the first thing bought with earned money — that felt different.

title: Take Care
description:
A senior colleague announced they're leaving. 40% salary increase at a new company.
Farewell dinner — everyone drank. Genuinely happy for them.

{name} watched the colleague's retreating figure and thought:
When is your turn? Or — do you choose to stay?

choices.text: Seriously start looking for other options.  (opportunity / uncertainty)
choices.result_text:
{name} opened LinkedIn that night.
Two positions worth noting. Wrote applications instead of closing the tab.
Making a choice — more nerve-wracking than expected.

choices.text: Stay focused on the current role. The time will come.  (stability / inertia)
choices.result_text:
{name} saved the colleague's number and went to sleep.
Connections carry forward. There's work to do here for now.

title: Late-Night Order
description:
Late again. 8 p.m.
Need to eat. Open the delivery app — delivery fee stares back.
Chicken: 20,000 won + 4,000 won delivery fee. Cup ramyeon from downstairs: 1,200 won.

{name} sits with phone in hand.

choices.text: Order the chicken. Overtime deserves some reward.  (self-reward / expense)
choices.result_text:
Chicken arrived and a coworker said, "Smells amazing."
{name} offered a piece. Eating together made the overtime feel less grim.

choices.text: Cup ramyeon from the corridor machine.  (save / health)
choices.result_text:
Ate alone in the hallway.
Salty, far from delivery, but hunger was handled.
Another day somehow passed.

title: Unexpected Kindness
description:
Dropped everything on the subway.
Documents, coins scattered.

The person standing next to {name} — without a word, bent down and started picking things up.
Couldn't make eye contact properly. Said 'thank you' — they were already walking away.

choices.text: Nothing special — go back to the phone.  (move on / missed moment)
choices.result_text:
{name} gathered the papers and put in the earphones.
But that moment stayed in mind for a while.

choices.text: Decide to do the same for someone else today.  (resolve / growth)
choices.result_text:
{name} helped an elderly man who was studying a map that afternoon.
Something connected in a chain.

title: A Seat at the Library
description:
Public library reading room.
Found a seat. Computer hum, pages turning, someone's keyboard clicks.
Everyone here is heading somewhere.
{name} opened a notebook.

choices.text: Focus. Study until it gets dark.  (growth / time)
choices.result_text:
Outside darkened before {name} noticed.
Understood something today. Not completely — but a little.

choices.text: Can't concentrate. Just sit here anyway.  (inertia / time spent)
choices.result_text:
An hour later — only the screen changed. Wanted to leave.
{name} packed up. At least came.

choices.text: Talk to the person sitting next to you.  (connection / social risk)
choices.result_text:
Studying for the Grade 9 civil service exam. Been in Seoul for three years from a smaller city.
"Me too, something like that." {name} said.
A brief encounter — but the same direction.

title: This Book Found Me
description:
A book picked up at a secondhand store.
Opened it without much thought — and stopped at one page.
A sentence that saw straight through {name}'s current situation.

Read it cover to cover, right there.

choices.text: Buy it. Going to read this again.  (investment / expense)
choices.result_text:
Three passages underlined.
One stayed in {name}'s head for days.

choices.text: Photograph the key pages and put it back.  (frugal / shallow)
choices.result_text:
{name} snapped the essential pages.
Knew even then that photos and reading are different.

title: Exit 2
description:
A busker in the subway corridor.
One guitar, one mic, small speaker on a cardboard box.
The music was better than expected.
People mostly walked past. Some stopped.

choices.text: Stop and listen a while.  (pause / time)
choices.result_text:
Stayed for two songs. When the second one ended, someone clapped. {name} did too.
A stranger's song — the best moment of the day.

choices.text: Drop 1,000 won in the case.  (support / expense)
choices.result_text:
Put a bill in. The busker nodded once.
Not quite gratitude — closer to respect.

choices.text: Keep walking. Running late.  (brisk pace / missed)
choices.result_text:
{name} stepped onto the escalator.
The music faded. Didn't look back.

title: Sunday, 11 p.m.
description:
The weekend is ending.
Work tomorrow.
Nothing actually bad happened — but there's a tightness in the chest.
{name} learned the name for this feeling later: the Sunday blues.

choices.text: Try to sleep early. For tomorrow.  (health / suppression)
choices.result_text:
{name} put the phone down and lay there.
Sleep didn't come easily. Eyes stayed shut anyway.
Tomorrow comes.

choices.text: Watch videos until early morning.  (escape / health)
choices.result_text:
Past midnight. Not even interesting — kept scrolling anyway.
Woke up heavy the next morning.

choices.text: Do something enjoyable. Cleaning, exercise, anything.  (self-care / energy)
choices.result_text:
{name} did the cleaning that had been sitting undone.
The room felt better. A small sense of control.
Good enough.

title: A Photo in the Chat
description:
A KakaoTalk message from a friend.
Baby photo. Newborn.
"This is my daughter. Isn't she beautiful?"

{name} stared at the screen for a long moment.
What does it feel like to become someone's parent at this age?

choices.text: Congratulate them sincerely. Send a gift.  (relationship / expense)
choices.result_text:
Navigated the baby department at the department store, a little lost — but found something decent.
Friend said, "Thanks, this is actually the most practical thing."
There are many ways to grow up.

choices.text: Send a congratulations message for now.  (compromise / relationship)
choices.result_text:
"She's beautiful — wishing her health and happiness." Sent.
Friend sent back a heart.
Brought the gift a month later when they met.

choices.text: Feel strangely distant. Not quite your story yet.  (distance / introspection)
choices.result_text:
Liked the photo. But it felt far away.
Someone who used to be in the same world had stepped into a different one.
{name} put the phone down and sat for a moment.

title: Done
description:
Nothing major.
A phone call put off for too long, a form that needed filing, a task left unfinished.
{name} got it done today.

No one knows. But — a quiet satisfaction.

choices.text: Move on. It was just the bare minimum.  (modesty / self-dismissal)
choices.result_text:
Added the next item to the list.
Still — today felt slightly different.

choices.text: Give yourself a small reward. Coffee.  (self-recognition / expense)
choices.result_text:
{name} ordered from a favorite café.
A small acknowledgment. That felt right.

title: The Neighborhood Changed
description:
Walking through a familiar neighborhood.
The old pojangmacha is gone — an interior design shop in its place.
The gopchang joint became a craft burger bar.
A real estate agency window shows new listings — prices higher than a few months ago.

Redevelopment, people are saying. Where did the original residents go?

choices.text: Look into nearby property carefully.  (information gathering / speculation)
choices.result_text:
Asked the agent. "You're thinking of getting in?"
Watching lines drawn on a map — {name} wasn't sure how much to trust any of it.

choices.text: Walk on. That money's not mine yet.  (resignation / opportunity passed)
choices.result_text:
Did a full loop past the old snack shop site.
Somewhere out there was the taste of the tteokbokki from years ago.
Gone now.

title: Past Self
description:
A notebook surfaced while tidying up.
Seems to be from second year of university.
"By the time I'm 30, I want to be this kind of person" — a list.

{name} read it line by line.
Some were done. Some still weren't. And some — {name} had no idea when they were given up.

choices.text: It's not too late.  (resolve / motivation)
choices.result_text:
{name} added one more item: 'Enter Gangnam by 38.'
The old notebook came back to life.

choices.text: That was then. Let it be.  (acceptance / resignation)
choices.result_text:
Closed the notebook. The self who wrote those things and the self now are different people.
Not bad — just a little lonely.

choices.text: Do one item on the list right now.  (action / small courage)
choices.result_text:
Something long put off — picked the one that could be done today.
Not remarkable. But moving that one thing moved something else too.

title: The Driver
description:
You caught a taxi late at night.
The driver glanced at you in the rearview mirror and struck up a conversation.
"You're young. What kind of work do you do?"

The talk went on for a while.
"Back when I was young, I said I'd make it to Gangnam someday too."
The driver said no more.
The city slid by outside the window.

choices.text: "I don't think it's too late for you, even now"  (comfort / empathy)
choices.result_text:
The driver smiled. "Haven't heard that in a long time."
Getting out, {name} wondered whether those words applied to you, too.

choices.text: Quietly look out the window.  (silence / reflection)
choices.result_text:
{name} couldn't say a word.
Getting out at the destination, the line kept echoing in your ears.
"I said I'd make it to Gangnam someday."
